d: Garden. Mixed choir of Guests and Gardeners of Count Asdrubale; then Pacuvio; then Fabrizio on one side, Baroness Aspasia on the other; and finally woman Fulvia.
Pacuvio and woman Fulvia.
Macrobius and the Knight Giocondo, who are advancing to alter together.
The Marquis Clarice, to whom the Count Asdrubale responds in imitation of the echo.
Count Asdrubale alone, observing if the Marquis Clarice has left.
Marquis Clarice is said.
Macrobio and the Baroness.
Donna Fulvia, ind Pacuvio.
The Count, thinking, slowly advancing, and sayings.
Fabrizio and the Count.
Fabrizio alone.
Earthly rooms adjacent to the garden. Game and Clarice, then Macrobio, then the Count.
Pacuvius and woman Fulvia; then the Baroness.
The Baroness and woman Fulvia; then Pacuvius return with Macrobio.
Garden, as above. Chorus of Gardeners, which starts immediately. Then the Marquis Clarice, who moves modestly away from the rider Giocondo; then Macrobio; finally the Baroness and woman Fulvia.
Back macrobio, then Pacuvio on the opposite side to sayings, that in the act of departure meet in Macrobio.

Said; then the Baroness and woman Fulvia; then Count Asdrubale disguised with some Servants and Marinars dressed in the same costume. Notary with others pretending to be people of the Court of Justice, and Fabrizio simulating an extreme affliction.
Internal courtyard in the Count's house. Clarice alone; then the Count and Giocondo not seen by her, as she did not see from them; then Macrobius and Pacuvius, the Baroness and woman Fulvia.
Fabrizio with an ancient sheet in his hand, jumping for joy; choir of Guests and Count's Gardeners equally glad, and said.
Internal courtyard, as in the first act. The Baroness, woman Fulvia and choir of Guests of the Count; then Macrobio and the Count on one side; the knight Giocondo and Pacuvio on the other.
Macrobius and the Baroness in the process of leaving, and woman Fulvia holding her back.
Woods... pacuvius with a rifle, and choir of Hunters.
I play alone.
The Marquise Clarice is said; then Macrobio, the Count and the Baroness.
Choir of Hunters advancing, and sayings.
Earthly rooms, as in the first act. Donna Fulvia and Fabrizio, then Pacuvio affannato.
Count Asdrubale and Knight Giocondo.
The Marquis Clarice all cheerful with a letter unsealed in her hand, and sayings.
Pacuvio affannate, and sayings.
Donna Fulvia and Pacuvio.
Macrobius, then the Knight Giocondo, then the Count and two Domestics, each of whom carries a sword over a kiss.

Interior of the village; different houses, and among others those of the Count with practicable door. View of the countryside. On one side picciola eminence. Pacuvio from the Count's house; then woman Fulvia; then Baroness and Macrobio.
Fabrizio, who descends from an eminence, and sayings. Several inhabitants of the village walk towards the countryside in the air of curiosity.
Said aside; the Marquise Clarice in military dress, a lieutenant, a sergeant, two Caporals and Soldiers; Fabrizio returning, village dwellers and Count's Servants, who remain behind. Military march.
The Baroness and Macrobius, Pacuvius and woman Fulvia, who are advancing.
Macrobio and Pacuvio.
Gallery. Clarice in military dress, Count Asdrubale and the Knight Giocondo.
The Baroness, then woman Fulvia and said; finally all, each in his time.
